Root cause: you created
  toolbox-context.json mapping home tools, but never exported the actual home tool FILES into toolbox/. The work
  laptop's toolbox/agents/ only contains work tools (from our earlier export). The home PC's agents/skills/commands only
   exist in your local ~/.claude/ — they never made it into the repo.

  Fix: export home tools into the same toolbox/ directory alongside the work tools.

  cd <wherever agent-mission-control is cloned>

  # Copy home agents (won't overwrite work agents — different filenames)
  cp ~/.claude/agents/.md toolbox/agents/ 2>/dev/null

  # Copy home skills
  cp -r ~/.claude/skills/ toolbox/skills/ 2>/dev/null

  # Copy home commands
  cp ~/.claude/commands/*.md toolbox/commands/ 2>/dev/null

  # Verify both sets exist
  echo "=== Agents ==="
  ls toolbox/agents/ | wc -l
  echo "=== Skills ==="
  ls toolbox/skills/ | wc -l
  echo "=== Commands ==="
  ls toolbox/commands/ | wc -l

  You should see counts HIGHER than what the work laptop exported (13 agents, 29 skills, 34 commands) because now both
  home AND work tools are in the toolbox.

  Then commit and push:
  git add toolbox/
  git status  # should only show new files in toolbox/
  git commit -m "sync: export home tools into toolbox for work laptop visibility"
  git push origin main

  Do NOT modify toolbox-context.json — it already has the correct mappings. The only thing missing was the actual files.

  After this, the work laptop pulls and both modes will populate correctly — the server discovers local tools from
  ~/.claude/ plus synced tools from toolbox/, and the context map filters by mode.
